solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Let your hair down for fox?

definitions.meaning: to relax and behave more freely is to become less tame, read as a two-word phrase
to fox someone is to baffle or confuse them

explanation.surface: A question about whether letting one's hair down is a fitting thing to do for a fox.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is BE WILDER, which is what letting your hair down amounts to.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the verb meaning to confuse, and the split phrase meaning to act less restrained.

clue.text: Wild animal 26 caught in club

indicators.note: the cross-reference and the cricket letter sit inside the word for a club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport
the solution at 26 across means an old boy, abbreviated OB
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A wild beast trapped inside a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is OLD BOY, used here in its abbreviated form OB.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobcat is a North American lynx, a wild feline.

clue.text: I spent two bits in academy

indicators.note: broken into bits, the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spent a quarter at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two bits' looks like a quarter dollar spent, but 'bits' alone is the anagram signal on I SPENT TWO.
explanation.definitionFit: West Point is the US Military Academy in New York State.

clue.text: Reveal information from head of law school

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken from law

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Leaking secrets from the dean of a law school.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is a well-known boarding school near Windsor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is an idiom for disclosing something secret.

clue.text: Scrooge's last trees? Humbug!

indicators.note: the last letter of the word Scrooge's is taken

parts.note: the yew is an evergreen tree
the ash is a deciduous tree

explanation.surface: Scrooge's famous exclamation in A Christmas Carol, applied to his final Christmas trees.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'trees', supplies two different trees side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean nonsense or rubbish talk intended to deceive.

clue.text: Overhauled Porsche not right for ages

indicators.note: a car that is overhauled is taken apart and rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged
R, the abbreviation for right, is removed

explanation.surface: A Porsche that has been under repair for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' takes R out of PORSCHE, leaving POSCHE, which 'Overhauled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochs are long periods of history, as ages are.

clue.text: Pop not buying mom and pop art?

parts.note: pop and pa are both informal words for father
someone not buying a home is renting one

explanation.surface: A father who won't purchase folksy small-business artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mom and pop' usually means a small family business; here it is literally mum and dad, whose craft is raising children.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising children is the skill practised by mothers and fathers, playfully called an art.

clue.text: Get into trouble with Christian skirting centre of Cairo

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a Copt is an Egyptian Christian

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter word Cairo is taken

explanation.surface: A Christian walks around the middle of the Egyptian capital and runs into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: Copts, Egypt's Christians, fit naturally with Cairo.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop it is British slang for being punished or getting into trouble.

clue.text: Put down drink on cupboard

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
press is an old or Irish word for a cupboard

explanation.surface: Set your glass down on the sideboard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppress a revolt is to put it down by force.

clue.text: Doting cooks dote best

indicators.note: to cook the books is to rearrange them, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Fond chefs make the most of loving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooks' looks like a noun but is the verb signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone besotted is infatuated, foolishly fond.

clue.text: Arrive unexpectedly — when seeds have germinated?

definitions.meaning: to happen or appear without warning
a crop literally comes up out of the soil once the seeds sprout

explanation.surface: Something appears out of nowhere, just like shoots after seeds sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to occur suddenly; literally, the harvest emerging from the ground.

clue.text: Try writing about air pollution

indicators.note: turned about, the pieces read from the end back to the start

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An attempt at writing an essay on air pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but signals reading GO and MS backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: Smog is a fog thickened with smoke and fumes, a common urban pollution.

clue.text: Arsenic taken by writer somewhere in Colorado

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A novelist poisoned somewhere in the American West.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspen is a ski resort town in the Rocky Mountains of Colorado.

clue.text: Entering a church, kiss the carpet

indicators.note: the kiss goes into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: a minster is a large church, often once a monastery's
X is the symbol for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is reprimanded for kissing someone inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet the' playfully suggests a scolding, but it is the rug.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a type of woven carpet named after a Devon town.

clue.text: Capital city regularly breaking hard ground

indicators.note: the alternate letters break into the rearranged word
ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of hard are reworked
every other letter of the word city is taken

explanation.surface: A town whose hard ground keeps cracking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital city' reads as one phrase, but only 'Capital' defines; 'city' is the source of alternate letters that 'breaking' inserts into the scrambled word.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: One's caught playing polo with flair

indicators.note: the letters are played about with, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A polo player is out after a catch, despite his stylish play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' hints at a cricket or polo dismissal; it means fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: An April Fool is a person tricked by a prank on the first of April.

clue.text: Drummer in Guadalajara and Saltillo starts finding English-speakers

indicators.note: the drummer goes between the two initial letters
the starts of the two Mexican city names are their first letters

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the drummer of the Beatles

explanation.surface: A Beatle tours two Mexican cities, finding English-speaking visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Guadalajara and Saltillo are Mexican cities, which suits the Latin American slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gringos is a Latin American term for foreigners, especially English-speaking North Americans.

clue.text: Fool around with language for sticker

indicators.note: turned around, the word for a fool is read backwards

parts.note: a mug is a gullible fool
Arabic is a Semitic language

explanation.surface: Messing about with a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool around' reads as one idiom for messing about; it splits into fool and a reversal sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum arabic is a natural adhesive from acacia sap, so it sticks things.

clue.text: Stop work to steal or kill

explanation.surface: Downing tools to rob or murder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers finishing work, pinching goods, and bumping someone off.

clue.text: Off-white colour that's to be expected

definitions.meaning: an undyed, oatmeal shade like unbleached cloth

explanation.surface: A creamy paint shade that nobody would find surprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the pale, undyed shade and the adjective for what is normal.

clue.text: Metal spearhead

definitions.meaning: a heavy grey element, symbol Pb
to head or ... an attack or campaign

explanation.surface: The metal tip of a spear.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the soft heavy element and the verb meaning to head a movement.

clue.text: Soldier in corps co-ordinated programme

indicators.note: the soldier sits inside the corps abbreviation

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in a military unit follows an organised plan.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is a British Army corps of engineers who maintain equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a systematic plan, such as a fitness or diet regimen.

clue.text: Tea's in order after last of summer wine

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after that single letter
the final letter of the word summer is taken
put in order, these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word as printed, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Tea is served after the end of summer, with some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of the Summer Wine' was a long-running British TV sitcom; the clue borrows its title.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: In a tizzy, so dear holds dear

indicators.note: a tizzy is a state of nervous agitation, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Flustered, the speaker's beloved clings on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dear' appears twice: once as fodder, once in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love and cherish them deeply.

clue.text: Accommodating grouse one brought forward

indicators.note: the letter for one is moved earlier in the word

parts.note: a grouse is a grumble or complaint
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A shooting party's game bird is brought forward to oblige.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' suggests the game bird; here it is the verb-turned-noun for a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being compliant means readily agreeing and going along with others.

clue.text: Prepared to embrace good little girl

indicators.note: the letter for good is held inside the other word

parts.note: made, as in a meal made or prepared

explanation.surface: Ready to hug a well-behaved young child.
explanation.definitionFit: Madge is a pet name, a diminutive of the name Margaret.

clue.text: Odd letters from dear friends have gone astray? Gone astray!

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters go missing, leaving every second letter

explanation.surface: Letters from loved ones have been lost in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd letters ... have gone astray' says the first, third, fifth letters vanish, leaving the even ones of DEAR FRIENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Erred is a past tense meaning made a mistake or strayed from what is right.

clue.text: Painter back on ship when saint goes down

indicators.note: in a down entry the abbreviation for saint drops to the bottom

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: An artist returns aboard as the holy man sinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German Surrealist artist.

clue.text: Bloody wound, my dear chap!

indicators.note: wound as in wound up or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An injured man is addressed with old-fashioned concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury that fits 'Bloody'; it is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Old boy is a dated, affectionate British form of address between men.

clue.text: Red conspirator in Rome meets obstacle

parts.note: Cinna was one of the conspirators against Julius Caesar
a bar is a barrier or obstacle

explanation.surface: A Communist plotter in Rome runs into a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a Communist, matching the conspirator; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is a vermilion pigment, the mineral mercury sulphide.

clue.text: Coffee blend somewhat lacking in strength

indicators.note: somewhat says only part of the following words is used, a hidden run

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A weak mix of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'strength' as the definition and 'somewhat lacking' as indicator; the answer means 'lacking in strength', so 'somewhat' alone signals the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble means weak, without power or vigour.

clue.text: Arrangements of points in space and time in elastic form

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters are moulded anew

explanation.surface: Space and time stretched in a flexible shape, as physicists describe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elastic' seems to describe spacetime; it is the fodder with T.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a lattice is a regular repeating grid of points.
